claims.text: Oxidation resistance in Cr/Al-enriched CoNiFeMn alloys is governed by selective oxidation of Cr and Al.
Selective oxidation of Cr and Al forms a continuous, adherent Cr2O3 and/or Al2O3 scale.
A continuous Cr2O3 and/or Al2O3 scale limits oxygen diffusion.
Limiting oxygen diffusion through the protective scale slows oxidation kinetics.
Increasing Cr and Al while holding other compositional variables constant will promote protective scale formation.
Optimized Cr and Al contents cause rapid formation of a dense, coherent oxide barrier.
The dense oxide barrier slows further oxygen ingress through a diffusion-limited oxidation process.
Diffusion-limited oxidation reduces overall oxidation kinetics relative to alloys that do not form a protective scale.
Formation of the protective barrier reduces degradation of material integrity.
Alloys with higher Cr and Al levels will develop a more continuous and coherent protective oxide scale than lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys.
Alloys with higher Cr and Al levels will exhibit slower oxidation kinetics, including lower thermogravimetric weight gain, than the baseline.
Alloys with higher Cr and Al levels will retain better mechanical integrity than the baseline after oxidation.
Lower-Cr/Al baseline alloys are expected to form discontinuous or non-coherent oxide scales.
Discontinuous or non-coherent oxide scales lead to faster oxidation and greater mechanical-property degradation.
The proposed governing behavior is expected to hold near 1000°C in air for isothermal exposures up to 100 hours.
Other complex phases in these multiprincipal-element alloys may influence oxidation behavior.
In-situ monitoring can isolate the effect of protective oxide-scale formation from effects associated with other phase formation.
